lessonRef.unitTitle: PF4 — Using Credit: What Credit Costs and What Aid Is
lessonRef.title: Defense and extension: grants, scholarships, and work study versus loans

focus: grants, scholarships, and work study versus loans
objective: Price the borrowing needed to close a fictional aid gap over its full repayment life, and defend a plan that mixes work, saving, and borrowing under a stated constraint.
scenario: A fictional applicant faces a $5,700 annual gap and must decide how to close it. The loan terms, wage, and figures below are invented for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional gap and loan terms in these directions

tasks.directions: If the whole $5,700 gap is borrowed, the fictional terms are 6.8% over 10 years — 120 monthly payments — at a disclosed $65.58 a month. Additional work at the fictional campus wage pays $13.75 an hour.

prompts.text: What is the total repaid if the full gap is borrowed?
What does borrowing the gap cost in interest?
What does each dollar of this gap cost if it is borrowed? Give the answer to two decimal places.

tasks.directions: Now price a mixed plan: borrow $3,500, earn $1,400 through extra work, and save the rest before the year begins.

prompts.text: How many hours of work at $13.75 an hour produce $1,400? Round to the nearest hour.
How much must be saved in advance to complete the mixed plan?
Borrowing $3,500 rather than $5,700 at the same $1.38 per dollar saves how much in eventual repayment? Round to the nearest cent.

Defend the mixed plan against the simpler alternative of borrowing the whole $5,700. Say what the mixed plan costs that the simple one does not, and name the condition under which borrowing the whole gap would be the better choice.

The $1.38 per borrowed dollar assumes the loan runs its full 10 years. Say how paying it off in 5 years instead would change that figure, and why the direction of the change is certain even without the new payment amount.

remediation: Use the fictional scenario and work one graded prompt at a time. For each number response, copy the given fictional quantities into integer cents, choose the operation the wording calls for, calculate, and check the result with an inverse operation or estimate. For each written response, make a claim and support it with at least one detail from the fictional scenario. Use these steps to check the method while keeping every final result in your own response.
extension: Build a third plan that borrows nothing, state what it requires in hours and advance saving, and say honestly whether it is realistic alongside full-time study.
